Overall, FS-TCCs experienced daily average solar insolation, temperature, R.H., and precipitation of 6.56 kWh/m2, 26.12 °C, 71.54%, and 0.95 mm, respectively. To serve as a reference, control samples were stored in a desiccator (25˚C, 10-20% R.H.) for the duration of the test and benchmarked at corresponding timestamps. The bespoke electrical testbed comprised a 3-D printed frame to hold the samples in place and featured conductive aluminum studs (circular surface area: 1.27 cm2) on either side of the TCC to measure its out-of-plane electrical conductivity. To prevent abrasion from the rigid aluminum surface, conductive circular Cu-filled silicone pads (area: 1.27 29/52 DE-EE0010241 Nicolas Gaillard cm2) were placed concentric to the aluminum surfaces during measurement. With the TCC sample in place and touching the conductive surface beneath (i.e., Cu-silicone pad and aluminum stud), the top conductive surface was lowered to make contact on the other side, and a weight of 3 kilograms was placed on the stage to provide a consistent compressive pressure during each measurement. The area normalized series resistance (R) (Ω·cm²: later referred to as ‘resistance’) was measured by connecting the four leads of a BioLogic-200 potentiostat to the wires soldered onto each aluminum stud for electrochemical impedance spectroscopy measurement (V =0V, V =10mV, frequency: DC AC 0.5 – 1 Hz). To ensure minimal contribution from external components, the system resistance (R<0.1 Ω·cm²) of the electrical testbed (i.e., without FS-TCC) was verified before taking the measurement set. Ten consecutive data points were measured at each timestamp, and the averaged data point was used to represent the out-of-plane resistance. For Raman spectroscopy analysis, the FS-TCCs were removed from their sample holders after the outdoor test was completed and placed under a Renishaw inVia Raman Microscope with a 532 nm laser (max power: 50 mW) and a spectral resolution of 2 cm-1 to analyze the sample at 1 – 5% of max power with an integration time of 150 seconds. The measurements were taken using a 100× objective lens over a Raman shift range of 100-3200 cm-1.
